correctness.rationale: For t=y+3z the least coefficient of a is C(t)=2(t−floor(t/3)), attained at z=floor(t/3). Odd a makes 2t invertible modulo a; C is nondecreasing, so the least nonnegative t for each residue gives its Apéry minimum. For a=2m+1 the even thresholds are C(j) and the odd thresholds C(m+j+1)+1. Consequently the even members form a prefix of each row and any represented odd residue has both adjacent evens represented. The only nonsingleton run in a row is its terminal interval, bounded on the right by the next multiple of a. A terminal length 2(m−j) occurs C(j+1)−C(j) times, giving the asserted 0-or-2 law. Subtracting the terminal lengths from the summed thresholds gives B1=2m²+m−2(F(2m)−2F(m)), with F(N)=sum_{t=1}^N floor(t/3); its three evaluations agree. The redundant-generator boundary a=3 has B1=3 and B2=2. An independent reachability census matched all 50 odd a=3..101, stopping at a consecutive members to certify the entire tail.
